title: Philippine Nurse Licensure Examination (PNLE)
disclaimer: Original practice items for educational simulation only. Not affiliated with PRC/CSC.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: In the Philippine health system, Primary Health Care (PHC) emphasizes:
choices: Community participation and accessible essential care
questions.explanation: PHC stresses accessible, community-based, participatory essential health care.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: Which Philippine program focuses on expanded immunization for children?
questions.explanation: EPI is the DOH immunization program.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Maternal and Child
questions.stem: A multipara at 28 weeks should be advised that fetal movement counting is important because:
choices: Changes in pattern may signal fetal compromise needing evaluation
questions.explanation: Decreased/altered fetal movements warrant assessment.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Maternal and Child
questions.stem: Immediate newborn care in PH facilities commonly includes:
choices: Drying, skin-to-skin, properly timed cord care, and breastfeeding initiation
Bottle feeding as first option always
Separating mother and baby routinely for 24 hours
questions.explanation: Essential newborn care pathways emphasize drying, bonding, cord care, and early breastfeeding.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: A client with hypertension on a low-sodium diet asks why. The best nursing explanation is that excess sodium may:
choices: Contribute to fluid retention and elevate blood pressure
Replace the need for medication always
questions.explanation: Sodium promotes fluid retention which can raise BP.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: The most effective single measure to prevent healthcare-associated infection is:
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene remains the cornerstone of infection prevention.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Mental Health
questions.stem: Which response is most therapeutic for an anxious client before surgery?
choices: Tell me what concerns you most right now.
questions.explanation: Open, exploring responses validate feelings and gather data.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Mental Health
questions.stem: A client on an MAOI should be taught to avoid foods high in:
questions.explanation: Tyramine + MAOI risks hypertensive crisis.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice V - Nursing Care Management
questions.stem: In the Philippines, professional nurses are regulated primarily through:
choices: PRC / Board of Nursing and related nursing laws
questions.explanation: Nursing practice/licensure is under PRC and the Board of Nursing.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice V - Nursing Care Management
questions.stem: When a staff nurse delegates to a nursing aide, the RN remains accountable for:
choices: Appropriate assignment, communication, and evaluation of outcomes
questions.explanation: The RN retains accountability for the delegation process and outcomes.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: In Philippine family nursing, the family is viewed primarily as:
choices: A client system and partner in care
A substitute for public health law
questions.explanation: Family-centered community nursing treats the family as a unit of care.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Positioning a client with dyspnea in high Fowler's primarily helps by:
choices: Promoting maximal lung expansion and easing breathing
questions.explanation: High Fowler's facilitates ventilation.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Maternal and Child
questions.stem: During the first stage of labor, nursing care prioritizes monitoring:
choices: Maternal-fetal status, contractions, and progress of labor
questions.explanation: Stage 1 care centers on labor progress and maternal-fetal well-being.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Mental Health
questions.stem: Priority nursing action for a client with active suicidal ideation and a plan is:
choices: Leave the client alone to rest
Ensure safety and initiate appropriate precautions/referral
Argue that suicide is wrong only
questions.explanation: Safety first: protect the client and escalate per protocol.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice V - Nursing Care Management
questions.stem: Accurate nursing documentation is essential because it:
choices: Is optional if care was given
Communicates care, supports continuity, and has legal significance
questions.explanation: Documentation is a legal and clinical responsibility.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: Incidence rate measures:
choices: Existing cases at a point in time only
New cases in a population over a specified period
questions.explanation: Incidence = new cases over time.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: A client with Type 2 diabetes should be taught that hypoglycemia may present with:
choices: Increased urination as the only sign
questions.explanation: Adrenergic and neuroglycopenic signs are key teaching points.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Maternal and Child
questions.stem: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for about the first:
choices: 18 months without any foods ever after
questions.explanation: Guidance commonly emphasizes ~6 months exclusive breastfeeding.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice V - Nursing Care Management
questions.stem: A unit tracks catheter-associated UTI rates monthly. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Tracking infection rates is QI/patient safety measurement.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Mental Health
questions.stem: Mild anxiety can be helpful because it may:
choices: Eliminate the need for coping skills
questions.explanation: Mild anxiety can enhance focus.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: In community child health, IMCI primarily integrates:
choices: Assessment and management of common childhood illnesses in a standardized way
questions.explanation: IMCI is a key child health strategy in PH community nursing contexts.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Which finding most suggests fluid volume deficit?
questions.explanation: Dehydration/hypovolemia signs include dry membranes and tachycardia.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Maternal and Child
questions.stem: In Philippine RH/FP counseling, informed choice means the client:
choices: Receives accurate information and freely chooses a method
questions.explanation: Informed choice is foundational to FP counseling ethics.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice V - Nursing Care Management
questions.stem: Which client should the nurse see first?
choices: Client with sudden dyspnea and O2 sat dropping
Client due for routine vitamin dose
questions.explanation: ABCs / unstable airway-breathing threats come first.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Mental Health
questions.stem: A therapeutic milieu on a psych unit emphasizes:
choices: A structured, safe environment that supports recovery
questions.explanation: Milieu therapy uses the environment itself as a therapeutic tool.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: Barangay Health Workers mainly support:
questions.explanation: BHWs are vital partners in community PHC delivery.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: Incidence rate best measures:
choices: All existing cases at one time only
New cases in a population over a period
questions.explanation: Incidence focuses on new cases over time.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Care of Healthy/At Risk Mother and Child
questions.stem: Folic acid supplementation in pregnancy primarily helps prevent:
questions.explanation: Adequate folate reduces neural tube defect risk.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Care of Healthy/At Risk Mother and Child
questions.stem: Immediate drying and skin-to-skin contact after birth primarily supports:
questions.explanation: ESSENTIAL newborn care promotes warmth, bonding, and breastfeeding.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: A client with vomiting and nasogastric suction is most at risk for:
questions.explanation: Loss of gastric acid predisposes to metabolic alkalosis.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: Nitroglycerin for angina primarily acts by:
questions.explanation: Nitrates dilate vessels and reduce preload/oxygen demand.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: Hand hygiene is considered:
choices: The single most important infection prevention measure
questions.explanation: Hand hygiene is foundational to infection prevention.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: Therapeutic communication that reflects the client’s feelings is called:
questions.explanation: Reflection mirrors feelings to deepen understanding.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: PhilHealth Konsulta is best described as:
choices: An outpatient primary care benefit package
questions.explanation: Konsulta expands outpatient primary care benefits.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Care of Healthy/At Risk Mother and Child
questions.stem: BCG vaccine is primarily given to protect against:
questions.explanation: BCG protects against severe TB disease, especially in children.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: Incentive spirometry after surgery mainly prevents:
questions.explanation: Deep breathing with incentive spirometry helps prevent atelectasis.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: In hypoglycemia, the priority nursing action is often to:
choices: Provide a rapid-acting carbohydrate if the client can swallow safely
questions.explanation: Treat low blood glucose promptly with appropriate carbs when safe.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: Before giving digoxin, the nurse should primarily check:
choices: Apical pulse / heart rate as policy requires
questions.explanation: Digoxin requires heart-rate assessment due to bradycardia risk.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: A family nursing care plan should be:
choices: Collaborative with the family’s priorities and resources
questions.explanation: Family nursing partners with the family’s goals and capacity.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Care of Healthy/At Risk Mother and Child
questions.stem: A prolonged second stage of labor increases risk for:
choices: Maternal and fetal compromise if unmanaged
questions.explanation: Prolonged second stage needs close surveillance and timely intervention.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: Informed consent implies the client:
choices: Understands risks, benefits, and alternatives before agreeing
questions.explanation: Valid consent requires understanding and voluntary agreement.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: The Glasgow Coma Scale assesses:
questions.explanation: GCS scores eye opening, verbal response, and motor response.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: Iodine deficiency disorders in communities are primarily prevented by:
choices: Universal salt iodization and related nutrition programs
questions.explanation: Salt iodization is a key public health strategy against IDD.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Care of Healthy/At Risk Mother and Child
questions.stem: The anterior fontanelle of an infant normally closes around:
questions.explanation: Anterior fontanelle typically closes by about 12–18 months.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: For adult CPR, compression-to-ventilation ratio for 1 rescuer is commonly:
questions.explanation: Standard adult BLS uses 30 compressions to 2 breaths.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: Oliguria generally refers to:
questions.explanation: Oliguria is reduced urine output.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice I - Community Health
questions.stem: Effective health teaching should begin with:
questions.explanation: Assessment of needs and readiness guides teaching.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice IV - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: Post-op priority immediately after anesthesia is often:
questions.explanation: ABCs remain the priority after anesthesia.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice II - Care of Healthy/At Risk Mother and Child
questions.stem: Lactational Amenorrhea Method is most reliable when:
choices: Exclusive breastfeeding, amenorrhea, and infant <6 months criteria are met
questions.explanation: LAM requires specific breastfeeding and amenorrhea criteria.

questions.subject: Nursing Practice III - Care of Clients with Physiologic and Psychosocial Alterations
questions.stem: Neutropenic precautions primarily protect against:
questions.explanation: Low neutrophils increase infection vulnerability.
